title: An app reports a playback problem to the operator's own server
description: Serves "Every failure is reported with its reason, never silent" and "what the viewer's player saw" (PRODUCT.md). Playback-problem reports from the app are stored only on the operator's server (D-20261127-playback-problem-reports).
acceptanceCriteria: A signed-in app sends a report of a playback problem, with the problem's own playback id if there is one. The contract declares exactly what a report may carry: when it happened; the app's name, version and platform; the player's name and version; the error the player raised (a code and up to 1,000 characters of message); the player's state (position, buffered seconds, measured bitrate and the version and tracks playing, by id); and, if the viewer wrote one, a note of up to 500 characters.

A report carries no credential and no media link. The contract has no field for either, an undeclared field is refused, and text containing a token, a playback link or a URL of this server is stored with that part removed. A test sends each and reads what was stored.
It is stored only in the operator's Postgres. Nothing in it is sent anywhere else, and it is not written to a log at Info.

An administrator reads every report, filtered by account, device, title and time. A viewer reads only their own. A report shows beside its playback when the operator follows that playback (JS-021, once built).

Reports are kept 30 days by default (`playbackReportRetention` in configuration) and are deleted with their account. Each device is bounded to 20 reports an hour, and each report to 16 KB; one over the bound is refused with `too-many-tries` and `retryAfterSeconds`.
A count of reports by app and error code is a metric.
Every capability it adds is in the published contract (JS-183) and passes its conformance check.
notes: Not a dependency of JS-194, the cutover. Ask of Octave, relayed by the owner: "Say what a report must carry for you to act on it (check it against criterion 1), whether reports are automatic, viewer-written or both, and that builds pointed at jellyscale send them here and to no crash service outside the operator's servers."
